Summary of what I saved:

This question was CORRECT (0.0), so no failure to fix. But one genuinely reusable pattern surfaced and wasn't yet documented: the single-series absolute-change variant of the bond-yield-table questions, where the span endpoints are given as HISTORICAL EVENTS rather than explicit years.

I added a new section to the existing `officeqa-bond-yield-spread-monthly` skill covering:
- The historical-event → calendar-year decode table (WWII end=1945, Korean War=1950, etc.)
- "Highest quality corporate bonds (Moody)" = Moody's Aaa column (not Aa / not generic corporate)
- Take annual-average yields, take absolute difference
- The legit-zero lesson: a 0.0 rounded answer is correct when levels are similar across the span — don't second-guess it upward (this echoes the same anti-overcorrection note already in the Pearson section)

I did not touch memory — it's at capacity (2058/2200) and every stored entry is a higher-priority fail-derived note. The reusable content fits better as a skill section anyway, at no memory-budget cost.

Done.
